skill.name: skill-forge
skill.description: Guides Claude Code and Codex users through a structured process for designing, validating, and packaging reusable AI skills.
skill.summary: Create, refine, validate, and package reusable AI skills with a structured engineering workflow.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: The static scan produced many high-severity hits, but reviewed evidence shows most are markdown syntax, placeholder examples, standard Claude skill install paths, or local packaging helpers. No prompt-injection attempt or credential exfiltration intent was found. One medium semantic risk remains because the enhanced workflow recommends npx commands that may execute remote npm package code.

remediation.issue: Enhanced workflow examples run npx claude-flow@alpha commands.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the package version, document the trust requirement, and require explicit user confirmation before running npx commands.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes placeholder API client code with api_key and bearer authorization fields.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that examples must never include real secrets and should use approved secret storage when adapted.

remediation.issue: Installation examples write packages into the Claude skills directory.
remediation.suggestion: State that users should inspect packaged contents before copying or unzipping into ~/.claude/skills.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Package Execution in Workflow Commands
semantic_findings.description: The skill documentation tells users or agents to run npx claude-flow@alpha commands. This can download and execute an npm package during the workflow, so it should require explicit user trust and version pinning.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines contain executable npx coordination commands, and npx may fetch and run remote package code. The behavior appears operational rather than malicious, so medium severity is appropriate.

content.value_statement: Creating reusable AI skills can become inconsistent when requirements, resources, and validation steps are unclear. Skill Forge provides a structured process for designing, testing, and packaging production-ready skills.
actual_capabilities: Guides users through intent analysis before skill design begins.
Defines use cases, success criteria, and workflow phases for new skills.
Explains how to structure SKILL.md, references, scripts, assets, and diagrams.
Provides validation and packaging scripts for local skill directories.
Includes quick-reference material for repeated skill creation workflows.
limitations: It does not guarantee that generated skills are secure or correct without review.
It depends on the user or agent to follow the validation workflow accurately.
Some enhanced workflow steps reference external coordination tools that may not be installed.
It focuses on Claude-style skills, so other agent platforms may need adaptation.

use_cases.title: Create a New Team Skill
use_cases.description: Turn a repeated team workflow into a documented Claude Code skill with clear triggers, resources, and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Improve an Existing Skill
use_cases.description: Review a current skill for vague instructions, missing resources, weak metadata, and unclear success criteria.

use_cases.title: Package Skills for Distribution
use_cases.description: Validate structure, prepare bundled resources, and create a distributable package for a local or shared skill library.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Skill Brief
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Skill Forge to help me design a Claude Code skill for this workflow: [describe workflow]. Ask only the questions needed to clarify scope.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Skill Metadata
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve discovery and activation for an existing skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Skill Forge to review this skill name and description. Suggest metadata that improves discovery while keeping clear boundaries: [paste metadata].

prompt_templates.title: Design Resources
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan scripts, references, and assets for a complex skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Skill Forge to design the resource structure for a skill that handles [task]. Separate what belongs in SKILL.md, references, scripts, and assets.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Full Skill Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before sharing a skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Skill Forge to audit this complete skill for clarity, activation quality, resource design, validation coverage, and packaging readiness: [paste or reference files].

output_examples.input: Create a skill for reviewing database migration plans.
output_examples.output: A structured skill plan with target users, activation triggers, workflow phases, required references, validation checks, and packaging tasks.

output_examples.input: Review this draft SKILL.md for weak instructions.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review covering vague steps, missing success criteria, risky assumptions, and specific edits to improve reliability.

output_examples.input: Prepare this skill for sharing with my team.
output_examples.output: A readiness checklist covering metadata, resource files, validation results, package contents, and remaining review items.

best_practices: Start with real workflow examples before writing final instructions.
Keep core guidance in SKILL.md and move detailed references into bundled files.
Validate every generated skill with realistic inputs before packaging it.
anti_patterns: Do not create broad skills that try to handle unrelated workflows.
Do not hide required behavior in scripts without explaining when to use them.
Do not package a skill before checking metadata, resources, and examples.

faq.question: What does Skill Forge help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create reusable Claude Code skills with clear instructions, resources, validation steps, and packaging guidance.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for reviewing current skills, finding weak areas, and refactoring instructions or resources.

faq.question: Does it write all skill files automatically?
faq.answer: It provides a process and examples. The user or agent still decides which files to create and review.

faq.question: Does it require external tools?
faq.answer: The basic methodology does not. Some enhanced coordination examples reference external tools that should be approved before use.

faq.question: Is it only for Claude Code?
faq.answer: It is designed for Claude Code style skills, but the planning methods can inform Codex or other AI workflow assets.

faq.question: How should teams use this skill?
faq.answer: Teams should use it to standardize skill design, review quality, and packaging checks before sharing skills.
